With 2.66 million total viewers, “ Jimmy Kimmel Live” topped late-night for the second week in a row this season. This time, it was for Kimmel’s week of live Brooklyn-based shows from the Brooklyn Academy of Music’s Howard Gilman Opera House.
This year’s trip to the Big Apple turned out to be the show’s most-watched Brooklyn Week in 11 years and top adults 18-49 performance in seven years. And in year-to-year comparisons, total viewers jumped from 2.20 million to 2.66 million and the show’s adults 18-49 ratings increased from 0.22 to 0.27. This represents a 21% increase in viewers and 23% increase in adults 18-49 ratings from last year’s New York City edition. Kicking off Sept. 28, “ Jimmy Kimmel Live ” earned 3.25 million total viewers and a 0.47 rating among adults 18-49, with the show’s best telecasts in three months. These numbers are based on live+same day big data plus panel ratings.
The week started off with guests Pete Davidson (“The Pete Davidson Show,” “How To Rob a Bank”) and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday before welcoming Howard Stern (“The Howard Stern Show”), Amy Schumer and Tom Morello with a musical performance on Tuesday. Billy Crystal (“860”), Mahershala Ali (“Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother”) and musical guest De La Soul took the stage Wednesday night. On Thursday, fellow late night hosts John Oliver and Seth Meyers shared the stage with comedian Robby Hoffman (“Robby Hoffman: Wake Up”). Brooklyn week closed with Paul McCartney (“The Boys of Dungeon Lane”), Sen. Bernie Sanders, Jon Stewart and musical guest Goose on Friday.
This week’s “Jimmy Kimmel Live” is back in Los Angeles with a full slate of guests including Anna Kendrick, Marcus Mumford, Mumford & Sons and Sophia James on Monday; Kerry Washington (“Animals”), Kyle MacLachlan and Sophia James on Tuesday; Jessica Chastain (“Other Mommy”), Malcolm Gladwell and Sophia James on Wednesday; Michael Douglas, Daisy Edgar-Jones (“Sense and Sensibility”), Remi Wolf and Sophia James on Thursday.
